task: predict defibrillation shock success (ROEA) from pre-shock VF ECG
note: Proposes 1D CNN on raw ECG. RF/kNN/SVM/AMSA comparison taken from authors' earlier paper with the same SMOTE preprocessing. Other = NPV. Acc 93.6 = mean of Sen and Spec, consistent with balanced folds.

task: predict type 2 diabetes from clinical attributes (PIDD)
note: Proposes CGLSTM; SVM/RF/KNN baselines. vs_none only via Table 5 ablation removing all preprocessing. Eq. 4 SMOTE description is nonstandard. Accuracy 97.84 exceeds sensitivity and specificity, so metrics are inconsistent; no arithmetic basis.

task: predict presence of heart disease from clinical variables
note: Transfer learning: pre-train on multi-hospital (Cleveland removed), fine-tune on Cleveland. External = zero-shot test on Cleveland site, same UCI family (authors' caveat). Mild imbalance (60/40). Table 14 ablation without SMOTE. DCA in Fig. 2.

task: predict fault-prone code elements in Java projects (BugHunter)
note: Sec II.6 states SMOTE applied solely to the training portion; Table V metrics nonetheless fit balanced test data (Rule D), so coded before-split. CV described inconsistently (10-fold vs eight segments). Seven learners compared.

task: classify upsilon states vs background in CMS dielectron events
note: Particle physics (CMS open data), multiclass, background over 90%. Compares seven SMOTE-family resamplers and weighted RF against plain RF; SMOTEN coded other-SMOTE-variant. Other = FPR, FNR, NPV. Single 80/20 split.

task: classify network traffic as normal or one of four attack types (NSL-KDD)
note: Text states SMOTE on whole data before split/CV, but reported test counts are natural and CV recall (90.15) is far below accuracy (99.79): coded nr. Smart-grid framing; NSL-KDD. No ET without SMOTE.

task: predict cell-penetrating peptides from aggregated physicochemical properties
note: Random oversampling with replacement to majority count (not SMOTE). Five learners compared; no run without oversampling. Reported RF metrics internally inconsistent (MCC .906 with accuracy .946), so no arithmetic basis. Student report.
